target_customer: Market research teams at consumer brands and academic researchers who run surveys
problem: Text survey responses were declining in quality and gave little nuance. Researchers wanted richer voice and video answers that were still easy to collect and analyze.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for voice and video survey collection and AI analysis
product_category: Market research and voice and video survey software

founders.name: David Ferris
founders.background_notes: Software engineer on real-time ad auctions at Google, then AI engineer at Uber, per his YC profile.

founders.name: Mitchell Catoen
founders.background_notes: YC profile lists a path from Google to Phonic.

competitors.name: Voxpopme
competitors.what: Video response platform for consumer insights and customer experience surveys
competitors.traction_then: Founded 2013, launched VideoCX in 2018, sold to enterprise research teams

technical_complexity.rationale: Recording, transcription and analysis of voice and video responses used off the shelf speech to text in 2020, so the hard parts were reliable capture across devices and useful analysis, not research.

defensibility.rationale: Survey tools are easy to copy and incumbent survey vendors could add voice. Some data and workflow stickiness with research teams but no strong moat.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Not copied in a way that killed it. Ad tech company Infillion bought it in February 2023 to add unstructured sentiment data to its measurement offerings.

market_need_then: The founders said survey response quality had been falling for years. Research buyers were paying for video and voice insight tools such as Voxpopme, which showed demand for richer qualitative data.

branding.domain_note: Used phonic.ai. A different, later voice AI company also called Phonic now holds phonic.ai, which creates search confusion with the original.

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain B2B research tone focused on respondent quality

brand_strength.rationale: Trade press covered the seed and the acquisition, but no sources show mascot, community or brand driven growth. The name later collided with another voice AI company.

outcome_analysis: Phonic raised a seed round of about 2.2 million dollars in 2021 led by Tola Capital, signed enterprise brands and university researchers, and was acquired by ad tech firm Infillion in February 2023 at an undisclosed price. The exit looks like a strategic tuck in for a small team rather than a venture scale outcome. Speech to text becoming cheap helped. Terms are not public.
notes: Company website in the directory is blank and the YC page lists none; the old phonic.ai site now belongs to a different company, so the original site is treated as dead. Search results also gave the launch as February 2021 versus an October 2021 announcement date; the seed closed July 2021 per BetaKit. Competitor list is thin because only one dated source was found. CB Insights and Infillion disagree on founding year (2019 vs 2020).
